The most useful output format depends on the application. Markdown is convenient for human inspection and language models, while JSON is better for preserving block types, coordinates, page indices, and confidence values. Text quality should be tested with normal paragraphs, headings, numbered sections, quotations, and deliberately varied sentence lengths. The goal is not to make the document visually complex, but to expose segmentation and ordering behavior in a controlled setting. A ten-page sample provides enough repetition to test pagination, batching, and page references without creating a large file. Document parsing systems convert page-based files into representations that can be searched, summarized, and analyzed. A reliable parser must preserve reading order, section hierarchy, paragraph boundaries, and page references while avoiding the accidental introduction of unsupported content.
